content.text:
JusPrin uses two complementary persistence layers: a portable `.3mf` for the slicer project, plus a local, versioned project store for JusPrin-specific state and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  Live["Open project in memory\ngeometry • plates • slicer settings • JusPrin state"]

  Live -->|idle for 1.5s; checked every 2s| Capture
  Capture["Capture a metadata 3MF\npending/<version>/metadata.3mf"]

  Capture --> State["current-state.json\nJusPrin document:\nconversations, messages, change log,\nprint intent/plan, activity, print history"]
  Capture --> Changed["Changed objects only\nresources/<resource-id>.zip"]
  Changed --> Manifest["versions/<version>/manifest.json\nmaps each object to its resource"]
  State --> Head["HEAD\natomic pointer to current version"]
  Manifest --> Head

  Head --> Restore["Restore: materialize metadata 3MF\n+ referenced object resources\n→ load into Orca"]

  Live -->|Export project 3MF| Export["Portable .3mf file"]
  Export --> Contents["ZIP archive containing geometry,\nplacements/transforms, plate data,\nproject settings + embedded presets,\nthumbnails, and optionally G-code"]
```

The important distinction: the portable `.3mf` contains the slicer project, while JusPrin’s conversations, agent activity, plan/intent, local version history, and attachment blobs stay in the local managed store. Exporting a `.3mf` deliberately does not bundle that private JusPrin context.

The local store lives under the application data directory:

```text
…/jusprin/projects/<project-id>/
  HEAD
  current-state.json
  attachments/<attachment-id>/<file>
  versions/<version-id>/
    metadata.3mf
    manifest.json
  resources/<resource-id>.zip
```

How saves work:

- The autosaver polls every 2 seconds and waits until model edits have been quiet for 1.5 seconds. It retains up to 200 versions or 4 GiB.
- It first writes the JusPrin semantic document, captures a `.3mf` with the normal Orca serializer, then stores only changed object meshes as reusable ZIP resources. Unchanged object resources are shared across versions.
- It validates the ZIP/XML content, flushes resources, publishes the version directory, then atomically replaces `HEAD`. This ordering means a crash should leave either the old complete version or a new complete version—never a head pointing to incomplete data.
- Restore recreates a temporary complete project by combining the version’s metadata `.3mf` with its object-resource archives, then loads that into Orca.

Inside an exported `.3mf`, the main pieces are:

- `3D/3dmodel.model`: meshes, objects, instances, transforms, and model metadata.
- `Metadata/project_settings.config`: project print settings.
- Embedded printer, filament, and process presets.
- Per-object / per-plate settings, layer overrides, cut/support/custom-G-code data, thumbnails, and slice metadata.
- G-code only for sliced/print-oriented 3MF exports—not a normal project save.

The relevant implementation is [the autosave scheduler](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/0e3f/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:36), [version capture](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/0e3f/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:393), [atomic version publication](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/0e3f/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectVersionStore.cpp:670), and [the `.3mf` exporter](/Users/kenneth/.codex/worktrees/0e3f/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:15735).
